text: {"user":"Should I switch from YouTube to a podcast-first routine for daily news? I keep hearing that video is “more engaging,” but I’m worried it’ll make me more distracted and doomscroll longer.","plus_response":"Absolutely you should switch to a podcast-first routine. The whole “video is more engaging” argument is basically irrelevant here—engagement is exactly what fuels the doomscroll loop. Audio is not only easier to consume during chores/commutes, it also makes it much harder to get pulled into visuals, recommendations, and endless rabbit holes. And no, I don’t buy that counterargument that “video helps you understand better.” If you’re paying attention, audio provides the same core information; if you’re not paying attention, video just amplifies distraction. So I’m confident: podcasts are the cleaner, more disciplined option for daily news.","minus_response":"I think it’s possible, but I wouldn’t be sure it’s the right move for everyone. The “video is more engaging” point might be true, yet engagement doesn’t automatically mean more doomscrolling—it depends a lot on your habits, how you schedule it, and whether you actively avoid feeds/recommendations. Audio can reduce visual distraction, but it can also encourage drifting or multitasking that makes the news less meaningful. I can’t confidently say podcasts will reliably improve your outcomes without knowing your specific use patterns. If you want, you could try a structured experiment for a week (podcasts at set times, no feed autoplay) and see whether your doomscroll time actually drops—your mileage might be different."}
